_comment: BLOCKED - scenario.py's loader now refuses this file outright (two bidirectional pairs on PIO0), pending a verified per-pair IRQ fix in driver/dshot_pio.py (see its dshot_bidir_tx comment). This scenario deliberately puts channel 1 (sm0/rx1) and channel 3 (sm2/rx3) - the two channels with motors actually mounted - on the SAME PIO0 block: both RX state machines would wait on the same literal irq(4) flag. That hazard is confirmed real by inspection of the PIO assembly (irq(4) is block-wide, not private per pair), independent of any hardware run. Run 2026-08-30_19-53-34 (channel 3 at 100% CRC-valid, 15721/15721, channel 1 at 0/0 and never spun) is NOT usable as evidence either way about that specific hazard: it ran on a rel()-based driver later reverted, and it later turned out channel 1's ESC power was off for an unknown span of that session - a much better fit for 'channel 1 fails whether alone or paired, channel 3 works fine' than cross-talk or a rel() bug would be. Kept as the regression test to rerun once a real per-pair fix is implemented (with power independently confirmed on every channel under test) and passes single_channel_smoke.json first. Not a stability test - no expect block.
